answer: A timber raft, lashed by the claimant and anchored with a stone at a named mooring, carries a sail painted with a fable only their household tells; the painted words are the mark no second raft can share. Two river wardens weigh the stone, check the lashings against the timber register, and confirm the anchor holds within four days. A drifting raft, a swapped stone, or a twice-anchored mooring voids the season, burns a 210-credit stake, and bars the yard two seasons. Forging 1,000 false rafts means lashing 1,000 timbers and painting 1,000 fables by hand; one honest claimant builds one.
